investigations.summary: Infra, not PMM or tests: both HA lanes died provisioning OpenShift because pmm3-ha-rosa #350/#351 (and #352 at 06:49) get CLUSTERS-MGMT-400 'billing account 119175775298 not linked to organization 1IQQauGmwrUH143LVRXQKXXnVHC at the aws marketplace'; #349 at 01:15 UTC was the last success, so the ROSA/AWS Marketplace billing link broke overnight and needs DevOps/account-owner action before any HA lane can run.

Same cause as #83/#84: PSMDB 8.0.32 refuses to start on the GitHub runner image ubuntu-24.04 20261015.610 (kernel 6.19+; mongod logs 'MongoDB cannot start: Linux kernel versions 6.19 and newer has a known incompatibility', SERVER-121912). All 37 failed package/GSSAPI jobs and both UI upgrade setups (3.6.0, 3.7.1) ran on 20261015.610; 0 of 105 jobs on 20261012.601 failed. Runner-environment issue, no pmm-qa or PMM defect; needs a PSMDB build that supports kernel 6.19 or pinning these jobs off the new image.

All 5 AMI upgrades fail 'PMM Server reports 3.10.0 / expected 3.10.1': pmm3-nightly-orchestrator passes pmm-submodules v3/VERSION (now 3.10.1) as PMM_SERVER_LATEST even for the 3.10.0-rc image; fix passes the RC tag's version instead.

PMM_PXC_TEST 'Verify dashboard after PXC Instances are added' found 5 empty panels (Ready to Accept Queries, Local State, Desync Mode, Cluster Status) against 3 tolerated on PXC Galera Node Summary for the client node; two CI-identical re-dispatches of PMM_PROXYSQL.yaml on main (3.10.0-rc server, pmm3-rc client, PXC 8.0) passed 4/4 each (runs 39392110719, 39392120917), and it passed on nights #80-#84, so this is an intermittent wsrep panel gap, not a PMM or test defect confirmed.

GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner images 20261018.* moved to kernel 7.0, where PSMDB 8.0.32 refuses to start (SERVER-121912); the fix makes rseq fail with ENOSYS for mongod so tcmalloc per-CPU caches stay off (Integrations: only the GSSAPI ol8 tarball job)
On RC nights the orchestrator passes the dev version 3.10.1 from pmm-submodules v3/VERSION as PMM_SERVER_LATEST, so the RC server's correct 3.10.0 fails the post-upgrade version check
